title: Tuesday Quick Tip
subtitle: The smallest player
hook: The smallest player on your team is often the bravest. Do they know it?
intro: They hear little one all season.
They play every inning hard anyway.
q1: Do you give smaller players roles that use their strengths —
q2: or treat every player the same?
q3: What can they do that bigger kids cannot?
t1: Every kid is different. But small players thrive
cta: Coaches — how do you build up smaller players?
ctaLines: Quickness roles. Praise grit. Same as everyone.
Special roles or the same path?
ctaPrompt: Share your habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
The smallest player on your team is often the bravest. Do they know it?
They hear little one all season. They play every inning hard anyway.
Size changes. Confidence carries forward.
Roles that fit their strengths or the same as everyone. Both can work.
How do you build up smaller players? Share your habit in the comments.
